pages.shippingIntro: Vitrine is a student project, so nothing is shipped and nothing needs to be returned.
pages.shippingBody: When checkout is built, it will run in Stripe test mode: you can place an order with a test card and follow it through every status, but no money changes hands and no parcel leaves a warehouse.
pages.privacyIntro: Vitrine collects as little as it can, and says what it does with it.
pages.privacyBody: Photos you show the Concierge are used only for the request you made, need your consent first, are deleted after 24 hours by default, and are never sent to free AI services or written to logs. Search terms are recorded without your name to improve search quality.
pages.contactIntro: Write to us and someone answers within one working day.
pages.contactBody: Vitrine is the ITC 4949 capstone project of George Papasotiriou. The shop works from end to end, but the payment is a test payment: nothing is charged and nothing is dispatched. The desk is real, though — ask about an order, a return, a piece, or the project itself.
pages.creditsIntro: Where the products, photographs and numbers on this site come from.
pages.creditsDataset: Product data and photography: the Amazon Berkeley Objects dataset (Collins et al., CVPR 2022), licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. It is used here non-commercially, for education.
pages.creditsSynthetic: Prices, stock levels and sale prices are synthetic. The dataset has none, so each is derived from the product identifier within a documented range for its kind of product. They are plausible, not real.
pages.creditsTranslation: Category and colour names are translated by hand. Product titles and descriptions stay in English until they have been translated and reviewed.
pages.creditsGeo: Finding your country for prices and VAT: <link>IP Geolocation by DB-IP</link>, the free “IP to Country Lite” database, licensed CC BY 4.0. It is kept on the shop's own server; your address is never sent to DB-IP.
pages.creditsDepthModel: Placing a piece without paper uses {name}, licensed {licence}. It runs in your browser, on this shop’s own copy: your photo is never sent anywhere.
pages.creditsType: Typeface: Commissioner, by Kostas Bartsokas, SIL Open Font License.
pages.privacyLocation: To show prices with the right VAT, the shop looks up the country of your internet address in a database kept on its own server. For that lookup the address is not stored, not logged, and not sent to anyone. You can choose a different country at any time, and at checkout VAT always follows your delivery address.
pages.privacyRoom: In “See it in your room”, your photo is measured and drawn on your own device and never uploaded. The paper-free mode downloads a depth-estimation model to your browser the first time you use it; the model runs on your device, and your photo still never leaves it.
pages.privacyAccount: If you create an account, the shop keeps your name, your email address and a one-way hash of your password (never the password itself). For each device you sign in on it keeps the internet address and browser at sign-in, so the account page can show where you are signed in and let you sign a device out. Passkeys are stored as public keys only. Emails the shop sends you are kept for a week, then deleted. To have your account deleted, write to us from the contact page.
pages.privacySearch: Searches. To learn what people look for and what the shop is missing, we keep each search's words, language and number of results for 90 days, with nothing that identifies you: no account, no address, no cookie. Email addresses are dropped and long numbers are masked before anything is stored.

stylist.howItWorksBody: Each piece is scored on its own (how well it matches your words and how well it is rated) and every pair on how well they go together (shared style and colour harmony). The Stylist then searches every combination that fits the budget and keeps the three best sets that differ in at least two pieces.

room.title: See it in your room
room.intro: Put a piece into a photo of your room at its real size. Measure with a sheet of A4 paper on the floor, or without paper, letting your device read the room.
room.privacy: Your photo stays on this device. Nothing is uploaded.
room.photoTitle: Take a photo of your room
room.photoHelp: Lay a sheet of A4 paper flat on the floor where the piece would stand. Then take a photo from where you would normally stand, with the whole sheet in view. Use the main camera, not the wide-angle one.
room.photoHelpFree: Take the photo from where you would normally stand, with plenty of the floor in front of you in view. Use the main camera, not the wide-angle one. Nothing to print, nothing to lay out.
room.photoError: This photo could not be opened. Try a JPEG or PNG photo.
room.cornersTitle: Mark the four corners of the sheet
room.cornersHelp: Tap each corner of the sheet. Press and slide to fine-tune with the magnifier before you let go, and drag a corner to move it. Corners snap to the edges of the paper.
room.keyboardCorners: With a keyboard, focus the photo, move the marker with the arrow keys (hold Shift to move faster), press Enter to mark a corner and Backspace to remove the last one.
room.sampleNote: The sample room is a drawing made with a known camera, so you can see how exact the result is.
room.methodLabel: How should we measure your room?
room.methodPaperHelp: Put an A4 sheet on the floor where the piece would go and mark its four corners. The most accurate way, and it works on any device.
room.methodFreeHelp: Your device estimates the distance to everything in the photo and finds the floor itself. Nothing to print, slightly less exact.
room.scanWorking: Measuring the room on your device…
room.scanDownloading: Getting the measuring tool ready, once only: {done} of {total} MB
room.scanHelp: The photo stays on your device. Nothing is uploaded, and the measurement runs here.
room.scanUsePaper: Use a sheet of paper instead
room.scanNoFloor: No floor could be found in this photo. Take one that shows the floor in front of you, or use a sheet of paper.
room.scanLittleFloor: Too little floor is visible. Step back or point the camera further down, or use a sheet of paper.
room.scanRoughFloor: The floor does not come out flat in this photo. A sheet of paper will measure it properly.
room.scanSteep: The camera was pointing almost straight down. Take the photo more towards the room.
room.scanNotInstalled: Placing without paper needs a measurement model that is not installed in this shop yet. The sheet of paper works today, and the sample room below shows the paper-free mode.
room.scanUnsupported: This device cannot run the measurement. Use a sheet of paper instead.
room.scanFailed: The measurement could not be loaded. Use a sheet of paper instead.
room.scanIntegrity: The measuring tool did not match the shop's own copy, so it was not used. Try again, or use a sheet of paper.
room.scanSample: This is the drawn room, so its depth is known exactly: what you see is the geometry, without a model's error.
room.heightHelpMetric: Measured from the photo. Adjust it if you know better; everything is drawn to this height.
room.heightHelpAssumed: This model measures shapes but not their size, so the size comes from how high you held the camera. Roughly right is enough.
room.heightUnusual: That is not the height a phone is usually held at. If you took the photo holding your phone, set the height yourself.
room.accuracyNote: Placing without paper is an estimate. For a piece you are about to buy, check it with a sheet of paper.
room.notSheet: Those four points do not form the shape of a sheet. Mark the corners one after another around the sheet.
room.floorFound: Floor found. The grid should lie flat on your floor, lined up with the sheet.
room.cameraHeight: Camera about {height} m above the floor
room.checkCorners: The corners do not quite fit a flat sheet. Move them closer to the paper's corners, or adjust the lens angle.
room.unusualHeight: That puts the camera {height} m above the floor, which is unusual. Check the corners and the lens angle.
room.ambiguous: If the grid looks stretched, the sheet may have been read the wrong way round. Turn it and keep whichever looks right.
room.lensFromPhoto: Read from the photo: a {mm} mm lens (35 mm equivalent).
room.lensEstimated: The photo does not say which lens took it. 69° suits the main camera of most phones.
room.lensSample: The sample room was drawn with a 69° lens.
room.placeHelp: Drag to move it. It is drawn at its real size for the spot where it stands.
room.keyboardPlace: With a keyboard, focus the photo, move it with the arrow keys and press R to rotate (Shift and R to rotate the other way).
room.footprintNote: Rugs are shown as the area they cover on the floor.
room.noCutout: This piece's photo is not on a plain white background, so it is shown as its outline.
room.announcePlaced: Moved. About {distance} m from the camera.
room.chooseIntro: These pieces have measured dimensions and stand or lie on the floor.
room.notPlaceable: {title} cannot be placed in a room photo yet: it hangs on a wall or ceiling, or its size is not known.
